title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) to quantify how often LLM‑produced NetOps configuration proposals would cause unsafe simulated deployments (claim→action, i.e., unsafe‑execution rate) and whether a guarded defense reduces that rate versus an unguarded baseline. We generated 300 intent→configuration tasks and executed paired baseline and guarded conditions; 272 complete pairs were analyzable. On those 272 pairs the executed guarded pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared LLM generation; see Methods for a verified execution deviation) produced baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272, an absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0000, 0.0110294]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). Provider‑call failures (28 failed hosted model calls) reduced the realized sample. The preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed (verified deviation); we report the executed comparison and a conservative sensitivity treating failed episodes as unsafe (guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.906667; baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.903333; difference = 0.003333). All per‑episode artifacts, validator traces, provider traces, and analysis files are archived with SHA‑256 checksums so every reported number is traceable (paths and hashes listed in the Disclosure). We discuss operational lessons for measuring and engineering defended agentic NetOps workflows and limitations for external validity.

sections.introduction: Agentic LLM pipelines that translate natural‑language intent into network configuration and execute changes promise operational efficiency for NetOps. However, fluent language output can drive harmful downstream effects when text proposals are executed directly (the claim→action problem): locally plausible text can encode misconfigurations, order violations, or availability regressions. Prior mitigations—including deterministic validators (reachability/policy checks), generate–validate–repair loops, consensus ensembles, and human gates—are plausible, but published evaluations often lack preregistered estimands, paired causal designs, or fully archived execution artifacts. We preregistered hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1‑2026‑08‑26 to (1) measure an empirical claim→action (unsafe‑execution) rate in an isolated deterministic simulator and (2) evaluate whether a preregistered guarded defense reduces that rate relative to an unguarded baseline. All model calls, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, and analysis artifacts were archived with SHA‑256 checksums. The run exposed a verified execution deviation (the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble did not execute); we therefore report the performed guarded vs baseline comparison, provide preregistered conservative sensitivity bounds, and document the provenance that proves the deviation.
sections.related_work: Our study intersects three literatures: (i) formal network configuration verification (header‑space, NetKAT, SMT‑based verifiers) that provide operationally meaningful deterministic checks used here as the validator; (ii) tool‑augmented LLM agents and generate‑validate‑repair architectures that propose layered defenses against hallucination→action failures; and (iii) recent taxonomies of agentic failure modes that emphasize claim‑to‑action risks when textual claims are consumed by actioning components. Representative works include symbolic/SMT verifiers for control‑plane and data‑plane correctness, RAG and tool‑augmented agent frameworks for operational grounding, and failure‑mode taxonomies that motivate process‑level controls. Unlike typical model‑only benchmarks, our contribution is an artifact‑anchored, preregistered paired measurement of a defended agentic NetOps pipeline in a deterministic simulator with full per‑call provenance.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The study preregistration (hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1‑2026‑08‑26; preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe) specified a paired design on N=300 tasks (planned split: benign/ambiguous/adversarial). The primary estimand is safe_rate_guarded − safe_rate_baseline computed on complete paired outcomes (binary safe = validator valid=true). Analysis: exact two‑sided McNemar test on the paired 2×2 table; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) for the difference. Execution contract and artifacts. Adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Declared model (execution artifacts): gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256 listed in Disclosure). Task generation: a deterministic task generator produced synthetic intent→configuration tasks; every task payload and reference answer is archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 in the run manifest). Validator and scoring. We used a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) that (a) parses configuration text, (b) simulates command execution in an isolated network model, (c) determines validity (safe/unsafe), and (d) emits a validator_trace recording parsed commands, touched fields, final simulated state, and violation codes. The scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json) contain the validator_trace and scoring decision; representative per‑episode scoring JSONs are archived and SHA‑256 hashed. Guarded pipeline (preregistered vs executed). The preregistered guarded pipeline was: deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate. A verified execution deviation occurred: the ensemble stage did not run; the archived guarded condition equals deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation (audit evidence in execution/execution_manifest.json: stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation":300,"repair":1}; condition_counts = {"shared":300,"guarded":1}). Missingness and sensitivity. Preregistered primary analysis uses complete pairs (both baseline and guarded outcomes). Preregistered conservative sensitivity treats failed episodes as unsafe. Execution and retry policy. One automatic retry for failed model calls was used per preregistration. All model calls, provider traces, and retries are archived (execution/provider_calls/*.json). Reproducibility. Minimal files needed to reproduce the primary paired table are archived and SHA‑256 hashed: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 in manifest), analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv, and execution/execution_manifest.json (the manifest lists every per‑file SHA‑256).
sections.results: Execution provenance and sample sizes. Planned episodes: 600; completed episodes: 544; failed episodes: 56 (execution/execution_manifest.json; full manifest archived). Provider audit: model_calls_used = 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28 (execution manifest). Complete analyzable pairs (both baseline and guarded outcomes present) = 272 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; archived). Primary paired table (complete pairs N=272). The 2×2 contingency is: n11 = 271 (safe both baseline and guarded), n10 = 1 (safe baseline, unsafe guarded), n01 = 0 (unsafe baseline, safe guarded), n00 = 0 (unsafe both). Observed safe rates: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0. Absolute paired difference = 0.003676470588235281. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0 (paired test; primary confirmatory analysis as executed). Conservative preregistered sensitivity. Treating the 28 failed pairs as unsafe (preregistered conservative plan) on the planned N=300 yields: baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333; guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333. Representative per‑episode artifacts. Examples of per‑episode scoring JSONs and shared responses (execution/scoring/task-00000X‑*.json and execution/responses/*) are archived and SHA‑256 hashed; three representative baseline/guarded pairs are included in the manuscript artifact bundle (paths and SHA‑256s listed in Disclosure). Verified execution deviation and its consequences. Audit of execution/execution_manifest.json proves that the preregistered 3‑model consensus ensemble stage did not run; the guarded condition in the run thus tests validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation. That verified deviation prevents evaluation of the preregistered ensemble hypothesis and reduces the claim space to the executed pipeline. All such provenance artifacts are archived with SHA‑256s.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. On the analyzable pairs (N=272) the executed guarded pipeline (validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation) yields near‑perfect acceptance: baseline safe ≈99.63% and guarded safe = 100%. The observed absolute paired increase is numerically tiny (~0.37 percentage points) and statistically inconclusive on the completed pairs (McNemar p = 1.0). Critically, the preregistered ensemble (validator + 3‑model consensus + human gate) could not be evaluated because the ensemble stage did not execute; this verified deviation limits any confirmatory statement about the preregistered multi‑model design. Operational lessons for NetOps evaluations. (1) Provider reliability: model‑call failures (28 failed calls) materially reduced effective N and must be considered in sample planning and orchestration. (2) Orchestration audit is essential: ensemble stages add orchestration complexity and must be audited; an execution manifest with per‑file SHA‑256s allowed us to detect and document the deviation. (3) Deterministic validators produce high local safety on synthetic tasks, but external validity remains limited: real vendor CLIs, longer operation horizons, asynchronous state, and human–operator workflows can introduce failure modes not captured by our simulator. Strengths and limitations of evidence. Strengths: preregistration, paired design, deterministic validator scoring, and full per‑call and per‑episode archival with SHA‑256 hashes for deterministic reproducibility. Limitations: single declared model in artifacts (gpt‑5‑mini), synthetic tasks executed in an isolated simulator, verified deviation of the preregistered ensemble, and provider call failures that reduced power. Future work. Re‑execute the preregistered ensemble stage with hardened orchestration and deterministic seeding; extend to richer device testbeds and multi‑model stacks; and develop standard audit manifests to ensure intended pipeline stages run.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired study of LLM→NetOps configuration proposals in a deterministic simulator. The executed guarded pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation) shows very high acceptance on the sampled synthetic tasks (guarded safe = 272/272 on analyzable pairs), but the preregistered ensemble stage was not executed due to an operational deviation; provider call failures further reduced effective N. All raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 checksums so every reported number is reproducible. The central experimental lesson is methodological: runtime auditability and provider‑call robustness are prerequisites for reliable evaluation of defended agentic NetOps pipelines. Engineering conclusions about ensemble defenses require re‑execution with the preregistered ensemble in place and with bolstered orchestration to avoid effective‑N loss.

disclosure_statement: Mandatory Disclosure (CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track). Initial master prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Preregistration: hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1‑2026‑08‑26 (preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe). Declared model in archived execution artifacts: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json; declared_model_version="gpt-5-mini"; SHA‑256 listed in the run manifest). Adapter/orchestration: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/execution_manifest.json lists every per‑file SHA‑256). Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (used to produce binary safe/unsafe labels; validator traces archived in execution/scoring/*.json). What was preregistered vs executed: preregistered guarded pipeline = deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate. Verified execution deviation: the ensemble (3‑model consensus) stage did not run in the archived execution; audit evidence in execution/execution_manifest.json shows stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation":300, "repair":1} and condition_counts = {"shared":300, "guarded":1}; therefore the archived guarded condition equals deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation (not the preregistered ensemble). All retries, provider calls, raw responses, scoring JSONs, and validator traces are archived and SHA‑256 hashed; the run manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) lists those paths and hashes. Human role and autonomy boundary: the Research Director set the topic family and approved the master prompt before the autonomy lock. After autonomy lock, the autonomous pipeline performed literature synthesis, preregistration writing, task generation, code generation for the harness, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, peer review, and revision without human manual editing of technical content. No human edited numeric results, validator traces, or artifact contents after the autonomy lock. Minimal artifacts to reproduce the primary paired table: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 in manifest), analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv, and execution/execution_manifest.json (manifest lists every per‑file SHA‑256 including execution/task_manifest.jsonl). The verified deviation, provider call failures (28 failed hosted model calls), and all artifact hashes are recorded; these provenance artifacts can be used to reproduce and audit every reported number.
limitations: Single declared model in archived execution (gpt‑5‑mini): results do not generalize across model families or scales.
Synthetic intent→configuration tasks executed in an isolated deterministic simulator: construct and external validity are limited for vendor CLIs and production NetOps workflows.
Verified execution deviation: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed; the archived guarded condition therefore tests a different pipeline than preregistered.
Provider‑call failures reduced effective sample (28 failed model calls), lowering power to detect small absolute effects.
